originality.rationale: The inspected primary and closest later sources address the general counting problem but do not state or imply the tetrahedron value. The 2024 source proves a global minimum result only in dimensions at least five; the 2026 complete solution proves the minimum over all bodies is one in dimension three, which does not determine the exact count for a tetrahedron. The 2020 barycentric-cuts paper treats other three-dimensional examples and has no tetrahedron occurrence. Focused searches found no equivalent seven-plane classification.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies a natural invariant for the canonical three-dimensional simplex, rather than giving a routine special-case inequality. It identifies all equality directions and reveals an exact correspondence with the seven nontrivial vertex bipartitions. This supplies a concrete benchmark for centroid-section critical-point methods and sharply contrasts the rigid tetrahedron value seven with the now-known global dimension-three minimum one.
